correctness.rationale: The center cones meet only along common right faces, so sending each apex to its base barycenter gives a well-defined equivariant strong deformation retraction onto the nerve. Distinct closed cube neighborhoods have intersection zero or two; each right face on at least three vertices has a unique center. In descending right cardinality its sole surviving strict coface is the cone over it. Same-size pairs are noninterfering, and their equivariant retracts can be made explicit: subtract the minimum barycentric coefficient on the free face from each coordinate there and transfer the mass to the fixed apex, using the linear homotopy. The all-dimensional residual incidence graph is the higher cube via the even/odd parity labeling. A pair of right vertices sharing a center has precisely two common centers, which form a unique square; the two cone triangles triangulate it. The parity lift preserves the odd diagonal and intertwines the full stated action. For n=1 no collapses are needed and the result is a filled square model of the interval. Reflections fix forced midpoints of axes, while a three-cycle forces its three equal coordinates to be all zero or all one in a two-skeleton. The remaining cube has dimension n-2; simple connectivity and its cell counts give the stated sphere multiplicities.

For translations all stable supports were edges and matched the claimed counts; for three-cycles the fixed Euler characteristics were 2,2,4,16 at n=3,4,5,6. These are finite consistency checks, not evidence by themselves of homotopy type. The supplied verifier was inspected, not executed.

originality.rationale: Supported distinct claim: the explicit full affine-equivariant identification, via a common incidence-cone intermediary, with the prescribed diagonal triangulation of the complete higher-cube two-skeleton and parity-lift action. The nonequivariant wedge, rational character, translation count and the unique-center collapse idea are not credited as new. The closest overlapping open-neighborhood collapse genuinely treats this complex after projection to one parity class, but ends in a different coordinate-selected complex on half as many vertices; it does not give the cubical intermediary or the lifted geometric action on the entire higher-cube two-skeleton. The two plausible general square models do not state the claimed equivariant conclusion under hypotheses covering all these cubes.
